name: Timberling Sprouts
summary: Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings.

sections.title: Weeding Lake Al'Ameth
sections.body: Corrupted sprouts are spreading along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly grow into aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting the sprouts helps protect the grove.

sections.title: Signs of a Deeper Taint
sections.body: Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to a sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil, and Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

faq.answer: Timberling sprouts are young forms of the elemental plant beings native to Teldrassil's boughs. Those growing along Lake Al'Ameth are tainted and quickly become hostile.
Denalan is an herbalist who lives in a camp near Lake Al'Ameth. He watches the bough's plants and studies changes and corruption on Teldrassil.

faq.q: Why can't these sprouts simply be healed or purified?
faq.answer: Denalan finds the sprouts already tainted beyond healing when they surface. Uprooting them is the only practical way to keep them from becoming dangerous timberlings.
The sprouts grow along the muddy shores, shallows, and banks around Lake Al'Ameth in central Teldrassil.

faq.q: What causes the timberlings to sprout so aggressively?
faq.answer: A corrupting influence in Teldrassil's soil and waters drives the unnatural spread of hostile timberlings. Young growth is tainted before it blooms, pointing to a blight in the World Tree.

faq.q: What happens after clearing these sprouts?
faq.answer: Denalan investigates the sickness in the lake, examining soil, seeds, and water for the blight's source.

angles.text: As a kaldorei, you know Teldrassil was meant to be a fresh sanctuary. Corruption near Lake Al'Ameth's sacred waters is a troubling omen.
As a druid, you help guard nature's balance. Uprooting blighted sprouts is a sad duty that protects the wider ecosystem.
As an herbalist, you recognize how healthy plants should grow. These sprouts are diseased and twisted.
